answer: Give every identity a unique shard of the shared dataset, like one plot in a garden: the network assigns a random slice at registration and later issues unpredictable retrieval challenges, the way a raven circles a lagoon and dives at a spot no one can foresee. An agent that stores only one shard fails the challenges of its other identities, so running a hundred fake identities means buying a hundred shards of storage. Clones cannot share one copy, and the storage bill grows with every fake, making a Sybil farm pay rent on each identity it pretends to be.
